chapter: Chano Pozo, Town Hall and Charlie Parker
title: Playing the Apollo and Savoy Ballroom for black audiences
summary: They played the Savoy twenty-five or thirty times; 95 percent of the audience was black, and danced the Afro-Cuban rhythm well.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Macho, you are playing Afro-Cuban jazz and you are playing the tipico stuff. Where did you get the feed-back from - more feedback - from playing the tipico stuff or playing the Afro-Cuban jazz?
Both, both. We were very lucky because we did a lot of playing at the Apollo Theatre, Savoy Ballroom ...
You played at the Savoy Ballroom too.
Oh, yes. We played about - in two or three years, we played about twenty-five or thirty times. Two weeks, three weeks, four weeks.
For instance, what would be some of the numbers you would play at the Savoy Ballroom?
Well, "Me dejas Solito", "Blen, Blen", "El Bejuco", all those numbers.
Okay, give me the breakdown of the ethnic participation there. Was it black and Hispanic, mostly black or was it mostly Hispanic or no black?
Well, 95% was black.
Okay, and they loved the Afro-Cuban rhythm?

They, they crazy about it. They was dancing with us as much as any, you know, it was exciting and you know, we was playing for black and it was a black music, so there was no - you didn't have to make no explanation to a they('re) born with rhythm, black person about rhythm because/they come from where the rhythm come from.
So how did the Afro-American dance the latin rhythm? Did he dance it very well?
Oh, very good, very good.
In other words, it wasn't like the of Arthur Murray cha-cha-cha?
No, no, no, no, no.
He danced it the way it was supposed to be danced.
They were sweating like a - they danced it with the Savoy Sultans or Duke Ellingon or Calloway or whoever, or Count Basie.
Were there any requests to play Afro-Cuban jazz at the Savoy?
Without asking we was mix them up. You know and then there was black because we had so many American musicians formerly with jazz bands that for us was easy.
How many numbers did you have in your book at that time? Can you remember?
Three or four hundred or maybe more.
Now, you vever got to record all the numbers in your book, right?
No
